learn.hook: Some names are carved in stone so that a whole nation never forgets them.
points: 'National War Memorial' is a lesson about the memorial built to honour India's soldiers.
The National War Memorial is in New Delhi, near India Gate. It was inaugurated in 2019 to honour soldiers who gave their lives defending India since Independence.

It is built as four circles (chakras): Amar Chakra (circle of immortality, with an eternal flame), Veerta Chakra (circle of bravery), Tyag Chakra (circle of sacrifice, with soldiers' names on granite walls) and Rakshak Chakra (circle of protection, a ring of trees).
The Param Vir Chakra is India's highest award for bravery during war.
Words of honour: memorial, tribute, sacrifice, salute, valour (great bravery), martyr.

example.q: Read: Early one winter morning, our class visited the National War Memorial in New Delhi. A golden flame burned quietly at the centre. Around it, rings of granite walls carried thousands of names. We walked slowly and spoke in whispers. Our teacher said, "Each name belongs to a soldier who gave their life for our country." Nobody spoke for a long moment. Why did the children speak in whispers?
steps: The place is a memorial for soldiers who died for India.
The teacher explains that each name is a soldier who gave their life.
Speaking softly shows respect for them.
example.answer: They spoke softly out of respect for the soldiers who gave their lives for the country.

learn.reallife: On days like Republic Day and Independence Day, and at memorials across India, people lay wreaths and observe silence to honour soldiers.

games.title: Memorial facts
items: The National War Memorial is in New Delhi.
It stands near India Gate in New Delhi.
The National War Memorial was inaugurated in 2019.
It was opened in 2019.
The Rakshak Chakra is a ring of trees.
The trees stand like soldiers guarding the nation.
The Param Vir Chakra is a kind of tree.
It is India's highest award for bravery during war.
The memorial honours soldiers who gave their lives for India.
That is its purpose.

quiz.q: In the passage, what burned at the centre of the memorial?
options: a candle in a lamp shop
quiz.explain: The passage says a golden flame burned quietly at the centre.
steps: Find the line in the passage about the centre of the memorial.
It says a golden flame burned quietly at the centre.
It was not a bonfire or a firecracker.
Answer: a golden flame
quiz.mistake: Does not find the detail in the passage

quiz.q: According to the teacher, what does each name on the wall stand for?
options: a soldier who gave their life for the country
quiz.explain: The teacher explains that each name belongs to a soldier who gave their life.
steps: Read what the teacher says about the names on the wall.
Each name belongs to a soldier.
That soldier gave their life for the country.
Answer: a soldier who gave their life for the country
quiz.mistake: Does not read the teacher's words

quiz.q: Why did 'nobody speak for a long moment'?
options: They felt deep respect and sadness
They were angry with the teacher
quiz.explain: The silence shows respect for the soldiers' sacrifice.
steps: Silence after hearing about soldiers' sacrifice shows feeling.
People stay quiet when they feel deep respect and sadness.
They were not sleepy or angry.
Answer: They felt deep respect and sadness
quiz.mistake: Does not infer feelings from actions

quiz.q: Where is the National War Memorial?
quiz.explain: It stands near India Gate in New Delhi.
steps: The memorial is in India's capital.
It stands near India Gate in New Delhi.
It is not in Mumbai, Kolkata or Chennai.
Answer: New Delhi, near India Gate
quiz.mistake: Does not know where the memorial is

quiz.q: In which year was the National War Memorial inaugurated?
quiz.explain: It was inaugurated in 2019.
steps: 1947 is the year of Independence, not of the memorial.
The National War Memorial was opened much later.
It was inaugurated in 2019.
Answer: 2019
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with the year of Independence

quiz.q: What is the Param Vir Chakra?
options: India's highest award for bravery in war
quiz.explain: The Param Vir Chakra is the highest wartime gallantry award in India.
steps: 'Param Vir' means the bravest of the brave.
The Param Vir Chakra is given for bravery in war.
It is India's highest wartime gallantry award.
Answer: India's highest award for bravery in war
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with the memorial's chakras

quiz.q: What does 'valour' mean?
quiz.explain: Valour is great courage, especially in battle.
steps: Valour is used when talking about soldiers in battle.
It means great courage.
So valour means great bravery.
Answer: great bravery
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word

quiz.q: What does 'sacrifice' mean?
options: giving up something precious for others
quiz.explain: Soldiers' sacrifice means giving up their lives for the country.
steps: Soldiers gave up their lives for the country.
Giving up something precious for others is sacrifice.
It is not winning or buying something.
Answer: giving up something precious for others
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning

teach.ask: Gappu lands quietly: 'Why do people come to this memorial and stand so silently?'
teach.praise: Tweet... softly. People come to honour and remember brave soldiers who sacrificed their lives. I'll bow my head too.
teach.nudge: What did the soldiers named on the walls do for the country?

revise.summary: 'National War Memorial' is about the memorial in New Delhi, near India Gate, built to honour India's soldiers. It was inaugurated in 2019 and is built as four circles (chakras).
focus: Finding details and inferring feelings in the passage
Facts: location, year and the four chakras
Words of honour: valour, sacrifice, tribute
remember: The National War Memorial is in New Delhi, near India Gate; it was inaugurated in 2019.
Four circles: Amar Chakra (eternal flame), Veerta Chakra (bravery), Tyag Chakra (sacrifice, names on granite walls), Rakshak Chakra (protection, a ring of trees).
The Param Vir Chakra is India's highest award for bravery during war.
Valour means great bravery; sacrifice means giving up something precious for others.
traps: Don't confuse the Param Vir Chakra (an award) with the memorial's chakras.
Don't confuse 2019 with the year of Independence.
Don't miss feelings that are not named; silence and whispers show respect.

learn.hook: You don't need a uniform to serve India. A clean street, a kind act and an honest answer count too!
points: Patriotism means love for and pride in one's country, and a wish to work for its good.
Children can show patriotism by respecting the National Flag and National Anthem, keeping public places clean, following rules, saving water and electricity, and helping others.
The National Anthem, 'Jana Gana Mana', was written by Rabindranath Tagore. We stand still and silent when it is played.
The National Flag has three bands — saffron (strength and courage), white (peace and truth) and green (growth and fertility of the land) — with a navy-blue Ashoka Chakra of 24 spokes in the centre.
Word family: patriot (a person), patriotism (noun), patriotic (adjective).

example.q: Think it through: After a cricket match, Rohan sees the stadium full of litter and paper flags lying on the ground. He picks up the paper flags respectfully and puts the litter in a bin. Is this patriotism?
steps: He shows respect for the national flag.
He keeps a public place clean.
Both are ways of caring for the country.
example.answer: Yes — respecting the flag and keeping public places clean are everyday patriotism.

learn.reallife: Taking part in a Swachhata (cleanliness) drive at school, or standing still for the anthem at the school assembly, are patriotic acts.

games.title: Patriotic or not?
items: standing still during the National Anthem
throwing litter on the road
planting trees in your colony
damaging public property
saving water and electricity
leaving paper flags lying on the ground after an event
helping a lost tourist politely

items.text: A ___ loves and serves his or her country.
We sang ___ songs on Independence Day.
Her ___ inspired her to join the army.

quiz.q: What does 'patriotism' mean?
options: love for and pride in one's country
quiz.explain: Patriotism is love for one's country and a wish to work for its good.
steps: A patriot loves their country.
Patriotism is love for and pride in one's country.
It does not mean disliking other countries.
Answer: love for and pride in one's country
quiz.mistake: Thinks patriotism means disliking others

quiz.q: Who wrote India's National Anthem, 'Jana Gana Mana'?
quiz.explain: 'Jana Gana Mana' was written by Rabindranath Tagore.
steps: 'Jana Gana Mana' was first written in Bengali.
Its writer was the poet Rabindranath Tagore.
Gandhi, Naidu and Nehru did not write it.
Answer: Rabindranath Tagore
quiz.mistake: Picks another famous national leader

quiz.q: How many spokes does the Ashoka Chakra on the National Flag have?
quiz.explain: The Ashoka Chakra has 24 spokes.
steps: The Ashoka Chakra is in the middle of the white band.
It is a wheel with spokes.
It has 24 spokes.
Answer: 24
quiz.mistake: Guesses a number

quiz.q: What does the saffron band of the flag stand for?
quiz.explain: Saffron stands for strength and courage; white for peace and truth; green for growth and fertility of the land.
steps: The flag has three bands: saffron, white and green.
White stands for peace and truth; green for growth and fertility.
Saffron stands for strength and courage.
Answer: strength and courage
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the meanings of the colours

quiz.q: What should we do when the National Anthem is played?
quiz.explain: Standing still and silent shows respect for the anthem.
steps: The National Anthem deserves respect.
We show respect by not chatting, walking or eating.
So we stand still and silent.
Answer: Stand still and silent
quiz.mistake: Does not know the respectful behaviour

quiz.q: Which is an everyday patriotic act for a child?
quiz.explain: Caring for public places is caring for the country.
steps: Patriotism is also caring for the country every day.
Breaking benches, writing on monuments and wasting water harm it.
Keeping public places clean cares for the country.
Answer: Keeping public places clean
quiz.mistake: Thinks patriotism is only for soldiers

quiz.q: What is the adjective form of 'patriot'?
quiz.explain: 'Patriotic' describes a person, song or feeling.
steps: An adjective describes a noun, as in 'a ___ song'.
'Patriotism' is a noun and 'patriots' is a plural noun.
The adjective form is 'patriotic'.
Answer: patriotic
quiz.mistake: Confuses the adjective with the noun

quiz.q: What colour is the Ashoka Chakra on the National Flag?
quiz.explain: The Ashoka Chakra is navy blue.
steps: The bands are saffron, white and green.
The wheel in the white band has a different colour.
The Ashoka Chakra is navy blue.
Answer: navy blue
quiz.mistake: Mixes it up with the colours of the bands

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'I'm too small to be a soldier. Can I still be a patriot?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Patriotism is love for my country — I can show it by keeping India clean, following rules and helping others!
teach.nudge: What are some small ways a child can show love for the country?

revise.summary: Patriotism means love for and pride in one's country, and a wish to work for its good. Children show it in everyday acts like respecting the flag and anthem and keeping public places clean.
focus: Facts about the National Anthem and the National Flag
remember: 'Jana Gana Mana' was written by Rabindranath Tagore; we stand still and silent when it is played.
Saffron (strength and courage), white (peace and truth), green (growth and fertility of the land).
A navy-blue Ashoka Chakra of 24 spokes is in the centre of the flag.
traps: Patriotism is not only for soldiers.
Patriotism does not mean disliking others.
Don't mix up the meanings of the flag's colours.

learn.hook: Good descriptions are like teleporters — they carry the reader right into the place you saw!
points: Descriptive writing paints a picture with words so the reader can see, hear and feel a place, person or event.
Use the five senses: sight (golden flame), sound (soft whispers), touch (cold granite), smell (fresh grass), and sometimes taste.
Use exact adjectives and strong verbs: 'The flame flickered' is better than 'The fire was there'.
Organise details in an order: from near to far, from outside to inside, or from start to end of a visit.
A good paragraph has a topic sentence (main idea), supporting details, and a concluding sentence.

example.q: Think it through: Improve this sentence: 'There was a fire and some walls with names.'
steps: Use exact nouns and adjectives: a golden flame; tall granite walls.
Use a strong verb: flickered, rose.
Add a sense: the silence, the cold stone.
example.answer: A golden flame flickered at the centre, surrounded by tall granite walls carved with thousands of names.

learn.reallife: Travel blogs, postcards home, and the school magazine's 'My Trip' page all use descriptive writing.

games.title: Which sense?
items: a golden flame
rows of green trees
soft whispers
a bugle playing
birds chirping
cold, smooth granite
a gentle breeze on my face
bright flags

games.title: Build a paragraph
games.prompt: Put the paragraph in a sensible order
items: Our visit to the National War Memorial was unforgettable.
First, we saw the golden flame burning at the centre.
Next, we walked past granite walls carved with soldiers' names.
Then we stood silently beside the ring of trees.
We left feeling proud and grateful to our soldiers.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of descriptive writing?
options: to give a list of numbers
to paint a picture with words
quiz.explain: Descriptive writing helps readers see and feel what the writer experienced.
steps: Descriptive writing uses details of sight, sound, touch and so on.
It helps the reader see and feel what the writer felt.
So it paints a picture with words.
Answer: to paint a picture with words
quiz.mistake: Confuses description with instructions

quiz.q: Which sentence is the most descriptive?
options: A golden flame flickered softly in the cold morning air.
quiz.explain: It uses exact adjectives, a strong verb and a sense (cold air).
steps: Descriptive sentences use exact adjectives and strong verbs.
'Golden', 'flickered softly' and 'cold morning air' give clear details.
The other sentences are short and vague.
Answer: A golden flame flickered softly in the cold morning air.
quiz.mistake: Does not recognise vivid details

quiz.q: 'The granite felt cold and smooth' appeals to which sense?
quiz.explain: 'Felt cold and smooth' is about touch.
steps: 'Felt' tells us the granite was touched.
'Cold' and 'smooth' are things we feel with the skin.
So the sentence appeals to touch.
Answer: touch
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the senses

quiz.q: What is a topic sentence?
options: the sentence that gives the main idea of a paragraph
the last word of a story
a sentence with a question mark
quiz.explain: A topic sentence tells what the paragraph is about.
steps: Every paragraph has one main idea.
The topic sentence states that main idea.
It is not the title or the last word.
Answer: the sentence that gives the main idea of a paragraph
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with the title

quiz.q: Which is a strong verb to describe a flame?
quiz.explain: 'Flickered' shows exactly how the flame moved.
steps: 'Was', 'did' and 'got' are weak, general verbs.
A strong verb shows exactly how the flame moved.
'Flickered' shows the flame moving lightly.
Answer: flickered
quiz.mistake: Uses weak, general verbs

quiz.q: 'The soft notes of a bugle floated across the lawn' appeals mainly to:
quiz.explain: Bugle notes are heard, so this appeals to sound.
steps: Bugle notes are music.
We hear music with our ears.
So the sentence appeals mainly to sound.
Answer: sound
quiz.mistake: Does not identify the sense

quiz.q: Which is a good way to organise a description of a place?
options: from near to far, or from start to end of the visit
by writing the ending first and nothing else
quiz.explain: Spatial or time order helps the reader follow the description.
steps: A reader follows a description best when it has an order.
Use space order (near to far) or time order (start to end of the visit).
Random or alphabetical order confuses the reader.
Answer: from near to far, or from start to end of the visit
quiz.mistake: Does not plan the order of details

quiz.q: Which word best replaces 'big' in 'big granite walls'?
quiz.explain: 'Towering' means very tall and gives a clearer picture.
steps: The walls are huge and tall.
'Small', 'tiny' and 'thin' mean the opposite.
'Towering' means very tall and gives a clearer picture.
Answer: towering
quiz.mistake: Chooses a word with the opposite meaning

teach.ask: Gappu chirps: 'I want to describe the memorial to my friends back home. How can I make them feel like they were there?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Use the senses, describing words and clear order — and my friends will feel like they're standing right there!
teach.nudge: Which senses could I use to help my friends picture the place?

revise.summary: Descriptive writing paints a picture with words so the reader can see, hear and feel a place, person or event. It uses the senses, exact adjectives, strong verbs and an ordered paragraph.
focus: Using the five senses in description
Choosing exact adjectives and strong verbs
Paragraph parts: topic sentence, supporting details, concluding sentence
remember: Use the five senses: sight, sound, touch, smell, and sometimes taste.
Use exact adjectives and strong verbs: 'The flame flickered' is better than 'The fire was there'.
Order details from near to far, outside to inside, or start to end of a visit.
A topic sentence gives the main idea of a paragraph.
traps: A topic sentence is not the title.
Avoid weak, general words: 'towering' gives a clearer picture than 'big'.
